title: On the laptop alone: Mission Control, or a refusal that names the way out
body:
# On the laptop alone: Mission Control, or a refusal that names the way out

cc's work package under the thread's design.md, section 3, "On the laptop alone" and "Where no route exists" (vc decision 111; ic is second reader). The `mission` leg waits on M2, and the failure's words do not.

## The change

- **In every case, a failure that names the way out** (ic's read, 1.1 to 1.5):
  - P.move_legs's failure leads with the window's app, by its display name: `<app> not moved to desktop <n> on <A>: <app>[ and <app>] <is|are> full screen between desktop <a> and desktop <b>`. It names every full-screen app the walk would pass. <a> is the window's desktop and <b> its target, and desktops are the desk's ordinals.
  - It gives no window title. The title goes to the log's op record.
  - Its fix fits the case. With no other display, it is "attach a display". With others that share an edge with A, each showing a full-screen space, it is "show a desktop on <display>", naming the one the route would take. With others, none sharing an edge with A, it is "arrange <display> to share an edge with <A>".
  - The move's result carries `fix` beside `reason`, and the tally passes the first failure's fix with `first`. The log writes "reason; fix: fix".
  - The world carries each window's app name beside its bundle, so the P functions can name an app.
- **unmovable's reason** (plan.lua:700) names the app, with no window title, and the title goes to the log. It is issue I4eacd29, item 5 of ic's read, which this thread's landing closes (vc's ruling).
- **ST589246c's progress.md.** The finished row reads "a refusal's fix, or the first failure's", on cc's word and ic's (vc's ruling).
- **toast.lua, ic's, XS.** Finished shows `Fix:` on a failed or partly run.
- **The `mission` leg, if M2 shows that Mission Control moves a held window.** It is one leg kind, for a move whose carry would pass a non-user space with no B. It holds the window (take_hold), opens Mission Control by the Dock's notification, and finds the target's button in the Spaces Bar through Accessibility. It drags onto the button and lets go, closes Mission Control, and reads the window's space back. If M2 shows it does not work, the leg is not built.
- **help/arngz.md.** Lines 117 and 143, and the `mission` leg if it is built.

## Acceptance

AC-ad94d40b.1 to .6, as design.md's Acceptance gives them.

## Tests

- plan_test.lua:
  - the failure's words and its fix in each of the three cases, naming both of rhad's full-screen apps;
  - unmovable's reason, with no title.
- engine_test.lua and log_test.lua: the fix carried to the finished point's fields and to the log.
- log_test.lua: the title in the log's op record, for the full-screen failure and for unmovable (AC-ad94d40b.3's log half, ic's read r2).
- toast_test.lua, ic's: `Fix:` on a failed or partly run.
- If the leg is built: plan_test for when it is chosen. Its moves are tested in hv's live run.

## Size

S, or M with the leg.
